2026 Top 25 Under 25: Honorable Mentions
stories.summary:
The Top 25 Under 25 is a collaboration by members of the Die By The Blade community. 92 readers ranked Buffalo Sabres players under the age of 25 as of August 1, 2026. Each participant used their own metric of current ability and production to rank each player.



Thanks to all 92 people who responded to Die By The Blade’s annual voting for the Buffalo Sabres’ Top 25 Under 25 list. Before we get into the list, let’s take a moment for the honorable mentions – aka, the players who didn’t make the top 25.



There were 42 eligible players this year. Several players on last year’s top 25 list aged out while others are no longer with the organization.



Let’s kick things off with a few players who just missed the cut for making the top 25. The scoring in the lower ranks is very close, and in some cases flawed too since a number of voters only ranked their top 10-20 players, and left the remainder of the names in the alphabetical order they were originally placed in. This means by default a Simon-Pier Brunet got more voting points than a Vasily Zelenov, whether or not one is better than the other. 



30. Scott Ratzlaff (G)



The goaltender will turn 21 in a month, and sees himself drop from 25th to 30th not because of waning performance, but more so the quality of prospects in the Sabres’ stable. Ratzlaff went 15GP, 3.10 GAA,  .913 sv% and a 5-7-2 record for the Jacksonville Icemen in the ECHL, and 13GP, 3.44 GAA,  .878 sv% and a 4-6-2 record for the Rochester Americans.  



29. Jake Richard (RW/LW)



The forward was drafted 170th overall by the Sabres in 2022, but after a breakthrough second season for Connecticut with 43 points and 16 PIM in 34 games, his performance dipped with 10G and 17A in 38 games, while racking up 42 PIM. He was in the honorable mentions last summer too. UConn lost to the Spartans (and their two Sabres, see below) in the first round of the playoffs, with Richard accumulating eight shots out of his team’s 42 in the 2-1 loss. 



28. Patrick Geary (D)



St. Francis grad Geary was drafted 172nd in 2024, and had a solid year at Michigan State University, where he wore the ‘A’ on his sweater. He had 2G and 9A in 35 games, with 70 PIM on the blue line leading MSU to the #3 seeding along with fellow Sabre blueliner prospect Maxim Strbak. Geary even scored in the regional final where they lost to Wisconsin, he’s definitely one to watch. 



27. Dylan Dumont (RW)



The 2026 188th pick is an intriguing prospect, scoring 28G and 16A in 62 games in the QMJHL. A scoring winger who attacks the center of the ice, Dumont was his team’s leading goal scorer last year. Drummondville coach Sylvain Favreau spoke in glowing terms of the youngster who turns 18 in a couple of weeks, saying he scored many of those goals off the rush and in front of the net by utilizing his best assets, his skating and soft hands. 



26. Zac Funk (LW/RW)



The Sabres acquired the forward in an ECHL trade this summer, sending Tyler Kopf to Washington for him. Funk, 22, scored 19 points (9+10) in 23 games last season with the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays. He also had two assists in 10 contests with Washington’s AHL affiliate, the Hershey Bears. The 6-foot-0, 210-pound winger has split his two professional campaigns between the ECHL and AHL after signing with Washington as an undrafted free agent at the end of the 2023-24 season, having led the WHL with 67 goals that year in 68 games for the Prince George Cougars.



Stay tuned as we break into the top 25 in a couple of days!

Which previous Bill (who’s not on another team and can still play) would you want on the 2026 team?
stories.summary:
Thought this would be a timely and realistic topic for discussion.



	 



	I’m on record as saying that I’d love to have Brandin Cooks back. I know his final play was extremely controversial, but I really do believe him and Josh had something going at the end of the year. I also believe he’d raise the wide receiver room, potentially become our WR2 and give us some insurance for potential injuries. I still want him back, even with the encouraging things we’re hearing from camp about some of our pass catchers.
	 



	That said, if I had to pick one previous Bill to bring back who’s not currently with another team, it’d be Matt Prater.



	 



	I’m typically very loyal to Bills players when they go through struggle times. But, Tyler Bass has struggled in one way or another for two seasons now. I realize there may be something going on behind closed doors that the fans wouldn’t know about, but he seems like such an unknown heading into the season.



	 



	Knowing the type of season we’re all hoping for, it’d be Matt Prater. Last year he kicked the GW against the Ravens and put us into OT with a clutch kick against the Broncos in the Divisional Round.



	 



	How about you, who’s one previous Bill that’s not currently with another team and can still play, that you’d want on the 2026 Bills?

stories.title: The Athletic QB Tiers (2 Panelists Voted Josh as Tier 2)
stories.summary:
The annual Athletic QB Tiers came out this morning.  Unbelievably, 2 panelists voted Josh as a tier 2 QB!  These 2 panelists must be incredibly spiteful or astonishingly stupid.  How do you not immediately dismiss any contributors to your story that claim Allen is not in the top tier of QBs in the NFL?!  I know it is a paywall article, but here is the link.  https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/interactive/nfl-quarterback-tiers-insider-rankings-2026/ 



	 



	How panelists voted in 2026



	Tier 1  - 48 votes



	Tier 2 - 2



	 



	Allen moved one vote closer toward unanimous Tier 1 status and could be the most feared quarterback in the league.



	“Josh Allen is unreal,” a defensive coordinator said. “He and Stafford are the two guys I would not want to play the most. Allen’s ability to make plays, be hard to tackle, put the team on his shoulders — when it’s fourth down, he is going to win.”



	 



	One veteran coach said Allen still has much to learn.



	“Josh Allen, with under 30 seconds left in the half, runs for a meaningless 12-yard gain and fumbles and gives up a field goal in a playoff game to go behind two scores against Denver,” this coach said. “Until he quits doing that, you can’t rank him as the top quarterback. That is one of the worst plays I’ve ever seen. Cost them the game.”



	 



	Others saw the positives.



	“The thing that jumped out to me about the playoffs last year was the physicality and the plays the quarterbacks make with their toughness, their size and their strength, particularly as they advance on,” an exec said. “Josh has got that. Obviously, it’s TBD with (new coach) Joe Brady, but one thing that those guys in the top tier do is, when you get off the bus on the road, the other 52 guys think they got a chance.”



	Allen led all quarterbacks in rushing yards (579) and rushing touchdowns (14) in 2025.



	 



	“He’s the real deal because he can do it as a dropback quarterback, and they do some run game with him,” another defensive coordinator said. “The way they use him is the way Baltimore has to use Lamar (Jackson) to get the most out of him.”



	A GM noted that the Bills have given Allen a strong defense and a strong run game, but not at the same time.



	“Josh is a 1 because he is the reason they remain competitive,” this GM said. “He’s so physically talented. But I’m ready to say he’s never gonna win a Super Bowl because their team’s getting worse around him, and I think his style of football is going to start breaking him down physically.”

We are now in the slowest point of the NHL’s year but trades still go down occasionally. Sabres rumors have died down too, even though a few have the team linked to kicking the tires on Kirill Marchenko of the Blue Jackets. He would be a huge addition to the team and an instant Alex Tuch replacement. He would also be costly. I’m guessing at least three good assets, with one of the young trio of forwards being involved, surely.

stories.title: Jedi Council
stories.summary:
Mad at Ads and Short on Grit Issue is Back



Hello fellow DBTBers, just a little Jedi Council to hopefully brighten your day. A new article for you to digest as we near the end of July, 2026 already. The poor kids here in Florida go back to school in just three weeks. I remember somewhere around September 7th for the start of the school year in Buffalo. I would have dreaded having to go back to school in the middle of August.



So away we go with a few topics of interest to me and hopefully you as well.



1. Casinos and Ironman Sponsorship?



As you may have heard, the Buffalo Sabres have joined most of the NHL by adding corporate advertising to their home and away jerseys. Color me disappointed to see our hometown team finally succumb to the almighty dollar. It wasn’t unexpected, but it’s still a little disheartening. I liked being one of the last hold outs on that commercialization nonsense. It was a point of pride that their sweaters remained untouched. Unfortunately, that’s no longer the case.



Former NHL Chief Operating Officer John Collins first brought the concept to the forefront in 2014, arguing that uniform sponsorships were inevitable. Unfortunately, he was right. Ads on NHL jerseys first originated as a league-wide initiative proposed by NHL executives and approved by the Board of Governors in August 2021 to generate massive new revenue streams.



Five years later, only two NHL teams (the Dallas Stars and the San Jose Sharks) do not have corporate jersey ad sponsors heading into the 2026-27 season. All other 30 teams have active jersey patch agreements. The Sabres will feature Seneca Resort and Casino on their home uniforms and Stark Tech on their road duds. Both will be small patches on the upper left side of the hockey jersey. That is Stark TECH by the way, not Stark Industries. No Avengers will be affiliated with the organization, sorry Marvel fans. 



Another company, Stark Naked, was turned down for obvious reasons.



Every NHL team now features an advertisement on their helmet, and most fans don’t seem to mind. Ads on jerseys, however, are a different story. To many hockey purists, they’re a blemish on the traditional beauty of a team’s sweater. I’m firmly in that camp as well.



With that in mind, here’s what the Sabres are presenting us with.







I know some people around here are not fond of the gambling industry that has really infiltrated the sports world in the last ten years. So the Seneca Resort and Casino sponsorship will never be appreciated by some. Visually speaking, at least the patch is also royal blue like the jersey and the lettering and logo are only white. There is thankfully no color mismatch between the two. A few NHL clubs out there sport colors on their ads in contrast to their team colors and it’s a real eyesore.



As far as the Stark Tech sponsorship on the road uniforms, the logo appears a little smaller than the Seneca home patch. The wording is a darker blue than the Sabres’ royal blue but barely noticeable from a distance. There is also some faint light blue and light green in the logo but the smaller size makes it hard to see. All in all, it could have been a lot worse. Neither patch is jarringly offensive, and eventually we will learn to live with them. I’m still going to bitch about it though, every chance I get. I absolutely loath the whole cash grab of having ads on hockey jerseys.



But if it’s going to be forced upon us, at least ours isn’t too obnoxious or embarrassing. No Chico’s Bail Bonds to be had.



2. True Grit



The Sabres have enough players who are willing to compete, but this offseason has left them with a shortage of players who consistently make opponents pay physically. The team dealt away size, strength and toughness in Jordan Greenway and Alex Tuch and also lost physical scrapper Josh Dunne to free agency. Buffalo added the monstrous Louis Crevier on the backend but no enhancement has been made to the forward ranks to replace that grit.









For years, Buffalo was viewed as a team that could be pushed around. Management recognized that and made a point of adding heavier, more abrasive players to the bottom of the lineup. They specifically targeted players who would forecheck, finish checks, and make the team harder to play against. Along with an occasional bout thrown in when needed. Last season’s Sabres were a team based on speed but they could throw their weight around too and answer the bell when needed. On paper, this year’s team may be even faster, but they don’t have as much muscle up front anymore. I worry that will cost them eventually, with the ‘roid rage goons of Tampa, always physical Boston and the newly hulked up Panthers just waiting to take cheap shots at them.



The 4th line of Krebs, Malenstyn and Carrick have tenacity and willingness to use the body on their opponents. All three will stick up for teammates but none of them are known for being a true protector on the ice. Beck is tough hombre’ but Krebs and Carrick don’t have the size to match their spirit. If the gloves come off, I say a quick prayer that neither player is going to get hurt and miss 20 games. Krebs in particular has a pattern of barely hanging on in his fights.



So where am I going with this? I believe the team is short at least one more physical forward. Somebody who forechecks hard, hits harder and is willing to throw down at a moment’s notice. A physical, go-to player the other team is always wary off. But the Sabres could also use a top-six forward to help replace Alex Tuch’s production too. Or at least a good portion of it. It’s highly doubtful they can bring in a 60-65 point player at this stage of the summer. But what about a 45 point one who also fills the grit and toughness aspect I’ve been going on about?



Enter the idea for Buffalo to aquire Utah’s Lawson Crouse. (yes, I’m still on this player for like 4 years now) The Sabres would be killing two birds with one stone trading for the big winger. He has all the traits I’ve been talking about that Buffalo is now short on. Crouse is a premier physical forward in the NHL, standing 6-foot-4 and 215 pounds. He is known for policing the ice and protecting his teammates, while dishing out heavy hits along the way. He can forecheck hard and obviously handle himself in a fight. He is the perfect addition for what the team lacks.



Crouse is not without skill or offensive ability, though, and that’s where the “two-for-one” value of acquiring him comes into play. Lawson has scored 20 or more goals in four of the past five seasons. Last year, he found the back of the net 24 times while adding 20 assists for 44 points, all while posting an NHL career-best +20 rating. He’s not the offensive dynamo that some of the fantasy trade proposals involving Buffalo have envisioned over the past several months. Realistically, Crouse is probably a middle-six forward on most NHL teams. That said, I believe the Sabres could utilize him very effectively on their second line. Surrounded by Buffalo’s high-end offensive talent, there’s even a chance his production could take another step forward.









Where Crouse really separates himself, however, is with the intangibles. He would instantly inject a much needed dose of size, toughness, and physicality into Buffalo’s top six while also serving as a protector for the team’s skilled players. Adding a forward who can contribute offensively while filling that role would address two major needs with one acquisition.



Lawson is also a regular and significant contributor on the penalty-killing unit, an area depleted by the departure of Alex Tuch. He frequently averages nearly three minutes of ice time per game while shorthanded. 



The 29 year old’s current contract pays him an expected annual salary (AAV) of $4.3 million. His multi-year deal is set to expire at the end of the 2026-27 season, at which point he is scheduled to become an unrestricted free agent. His actual cap hit this year is only $3.9 million which the Sabres could easily finagle into the lineup. Any deal would likely involve Crouse signing an extension. I imagine he would be looking for something along the lines of $6-7 million per season and at least a five year deal which Buffalo could afford with extra cap space next year. He would be worth it in my opinion.



I feel most of us would like to add a goal scorer while also bringing in a banger to replace what we have lost. Crouse does that with one move from GMJK. I won’t speculate on what it would take to acquire him. Most trade ideas are shot down anyways as either too much or not enough to give up. If I’m the Sabres’ brass however, I’m considering what some goofy “writer” from this forum is pushing. Or even some intern named T. McGee. Buffalo has taken a hit this offseason both in toughness and offense. The young talent of Kulich, Ostlund and Helenius could certainly be a fill-in factor from within. But adding an experienced, physical forward and a proven goal scorer would add an extra layer of protection to the defending Atlantic Division Champions.



So will this actually come to fruition? Like most hopeful deals made by fans, probably not. Buffalo’s GM may be off parasailing right now or on his 5th cocktail in Aruba. But I feel that this move would address both problems the Sabres’ face amongst the forward ranks. To me, they are still short an experienced scoring forward and some overall heavy sandpaper. This would be a great option to fill both those needs.



If you made it this far, I hope everyone is enjoying their summer. The NHL regular season kicks off in only about 9 more weeks…

stories.title: Pop Quiz, Hotshot! 2025-26 Sabres Edition
stories.summary:
A Magical Season to Remember in Return to the Playoffs



Last season’s Buffalo Sabres sure was a wild ride. The year started like business as usual with Buffalo in the lower half of the league before bottoming out at one point. Then something clicked as the team took off and never looked back, inching out the Atlantic Division title over always tough Tampa Bay and upstart Montreal. That led to their first playoff appearance in forever, then a six game series win over Boston before eventually falling in seven games to the Habs. The Sabres were an OT win away from being in the final four. Just crazy to contemplate, even now.



As we all wait on a potential roster move/upgrade from Jarmo and the Sabres’ brass, put your thinking caps on and see how well you remember the events of this past season. Here is a ten question pop quiz, answer honest and see how you score. Just ten questions in total, good luck! The answer key is at the bottom.



1. Lightning Crashes



In the fight filled, high scoring 8-7 victory over Tampa Bay, which Buffalo players scored the late goal to tie it and the even later goal to win it?



A. Zucker and Dahlin B. Tuch and Dahlin C. Zucker and Doan D. Tuch and Doan



2. A Perfect 10



On December 31st, 2025, the Buffalo Sabres defeated the Dallas Stars 4-1. It was their 10th win in a row. Which Sabre scored two third period goals to cement the win?



A. Benson B. Tuch C. Ostlund D. Thompson



3. Plus Sized



Mattias Samuelsson had the best plus/minus on the team at +41. Who had the 2nd best plus/minus?



A. Tuch B. McLeod C. Benson D. Metsa



4. Zero Hour



How many shutouts did the Sabres record during the 2025-26 regular season?



A. Three B. Four C. Five D. Six



5. Take Your Shot



Back in March, the Sabres beat the Sharks 5-0 in San Jose with a minimal number of shots on goal. 5 goals on how many shots?



A. 10 B. 12 C. 14 D. 16



6. It’s All About the Percentages



Which Sabres’ defenseman had the highest shooting percentage among Buffalo defenders last season?



A. Samuelsson B. Byram C. Power D. Dahlin



7. Playoffs? You Kidding Me?



How many Buffalo players scored 10 or more points in their 13 game playoff run?



A. Two B. Three C. Four D. Five



8. He Shoots, He Scores!



What was the most goals scored in a single game by the Sabres during the 2025–26 NHL regular season?



A. Eight (once) B. Eight (twice) C. Nine D. Ten



9. Everybody Gonna Jump For Joy



Jack Quinn set a career high for goals, assists and points last season. How many points in total?



A. 45 B. 50 C. 51 D. 55



10. Three’s Company



Buffalo secured three wins against four divisional rivals this past season. Which one listed below is NOT one of those teams?



A. Toronto B. Boston C. Tampa D. Ottawa



That is a wrap, my friends. All done, you are! The answer key is below. How did you do?









Answer Key




The answer is C. Zucker tied it on a partial breakaway and Doan won it on the rebound after Dahlin hit the post.



The answer is D. TNT capped the game with 2 third period goals.



The answer is C. Benny was a +27 on the season. McLeod was +25 in third place.



The answer is C again. The Sabres had 5 shutouts with all three goalies chipping in. Lyon had three with UPL and Ellis notching one each.



The answer is D. Buffalo finished the game with 5 goals on just 16 shots.



The answer is A. Samuelsson was 11.9% (13 goals on 109 shots)



The answer is B. Three players scored at least 10 points. Thompson had 15 (5-10) Dahlin had 14 (4-10) and Doan had 10. (3-7)



The answer is C. Buffalo layeth the smack down on Chicago during a 9-3 win for their highest goal total of the year. They did score 8 goals twice though, against Tampa and Ottawa.



The answer is C. Quinn scored 51 points on the year. (20 goals, 31 assists)



The answer is D. The Sabres had three wins each against Toronto, Boston, Tampa and FLORIDA, not Ottawa.

stories.title: Peyton’s Place: Krebs Signs for Four More Years in Buffalo
stories.summary:
The 5th Year Sabre Had a Career High 39 Points Last Year



Well, that was a little more difficult than expected. And expensive from most points of view. Peyton Krebs had to file for arbitration in order to come to an agreement with Buffalo but thankfully the two sides settled today before that came to fruition. It was a long and challenging process though.



Peyton “Swiss army knife” Krebs has signed to remain in Buffalo for the next four years. The versatile forward finally joins Zach Benson and Beck Malenstyn (and Olen Zellweger) as recent Sabres’ RFAs who have inked a contact to remain with the Blue and Gold.



Peyton’s deal is officially for $4.5 million per season, substantially higher than most estimates. But the deal has more term than expected as well, which should balance some cost with the cap later. 



Krebs has stated publicly that his family loves it here and he wants too win a Cup in Buffalo. That is fine by me, and all of Sabres’ fandom I’m sure. Krebs is a valuable resource to have. He is not great at any one thing but is good at many. We saw more offense from him this past season than ever before. He plays sound defensively and wins many puck battles. He has a big heart on the ice, works his ass off and is an underrated leader for this team. He can play up and down the lineup and doesn’t look out of place. And he never backs down from adversity.









With Buffalo still in need of possible top-six help in the forward ranks, Krebs could still be a trade piece. Even moreso with the higher than expected contract and the difficult negotiations each side just had. The Sabres are heavy in the bottom-six and at least two forwards could be shipped out to make room for the bigger fish. If so, I hope Krebs is not one of them. Lindy and Jarmo seem to love the player also. He has great tenacity and spirit and willingness to battle. He, along with Josh Doan and Zach Benson, are the kind of players that Buffalo needs more of.



His price tag is certainly above expectations. Hopefully his output will be the same way.
